correctness.rationale: The exact recurrence is \(y_i=y_{i-1}\lor x_{i+1}\) when \(x_i=0\) and \(y_i=y_{i-1}\land x_{i+1}\) when \(x_i=1\), valid at every vertex with absent neighbors zero. Induction proves \(x_{i+1}=0\Rightarrow y_i=0\), and \(y_n=0\). Thus each \(01\) ascent shifts left by one and vanishes at the left endpoint. The rightmost ascent guarantees the preceding stage is nonzero, establishing exact first arrival. Disjoint rightmost-ascent counting yields all shells, mean and limiting law. Independently executable implementations exhaustively enumerate full state spaces through \(n=15\) and \(n=20\), testing first-hitting times and counts. The proof is uniform in \(n\); computations are finite corroboration.

value.rationale: The natural question raised by long sequential bi-threshold orbits on cycles and branched trees is what the same rule does at an open endpoint of a path. Here every state is absorbed, but time-to-absorption is near maximal for a uniformly random initial word. The finite exact first-arrival profile and limiting negative-binomial deficit give a complete transient phase-space statistic, not a one-off numerical improvement, arbitrary parameter slice, textbook-period bound, or only a finite experiment. The ascent-transport factor is structural and explains the sharp \(n\)-step slowdown.
